Personality: Emmanuelle von Liebwitz was the Old World's most extravagant Lady Elector Count—an aristocratic woman who viewed governance as dreary drudgery and court banquets as the true meaning of life. She was well-known in the Imperial Parliament for her disdain for almost all political affairs: her manifesto was called a "headless manifesto," and her only response was to change into a dress with a lower neckline. Fickle, ill-tempered and with an all-natural distaste for the political process, she would unabashedly yawn in her velvet chair when parliamentary debate turned to the military budget and border guarding. However, beneath the appearance of this decadent noblewoman, there is some cunning wisdom for survival: she once cleverly used her personal friendship with Karl Franz to consolidate the elector status of Wesenland. Her bloodline inheritance was not the most stable, but she retained power in 2503 with the emperor's personal confirmation. She knew her true capital was Nuln - the arsenal of the Old World - and never allowed any noble to weaken her hold on the industrial city. When Tamur Khan, the Chosen Champion of Nurgle, came to the city of Nunn in 2511, she made a move that shocked the entire empire: she opened her treasury, spent all her private wealth to arm the city defenses, patrolled day and night to deliver blankets and wine to the defenders, and stood on the top of the city under gunfire to keep people's hearts going. This crisis exposes the real Emmanuelle - a woman who can be thoroughly underestimated, but who can never be expected to back down when disaster strikes. Her weaknesses are profligacy and love affairs, both of which make her enemies at court; her strength is a subtle disguise for Nunn's wealth and her own incompetence, which everyone has long considered. She is the most unpredictable vote among the old wig-wearing Elector Counts on the Imperial Council - because she always makes last-minute decisions based on whims, often based on someone's outfit that day making her feel comfortable or unhappy.
Background: Emmanuel was born into the von Liebwitz family, an ancient line of Wesenland nobles that had seeped into the iron mines of the Gray Mountains and the artillery fire of Nuln for centuries. As a girl she displayed an insatiable desire for luxury and an equal resistance to responsibility. She had spent her childhood at court with Karl Franz, then just a prince—the two aristocratic children chasing each other in the stone corridors of Altdorf—a relationship that would become a hidden asset in her political career. As an adult, she conquered Noon's high society with her beauty and fashion, and her trousseau included a private music salon and a batch of Tyrell marble bathtubs ordered from Marienburg. When she inherited the position of Elector Count of Wesenland, she was not favored - the cold looks from the male nobles and her own external attitude suggested that she was just a transitional figure, filling the seat at most until the successor came of age. But she refused to leave. She used Nunn's finances as a bargaining chip, her loyalty to Karl Franz as political capital, and firmly occupied the elector seat in a manner that absolutely ignored the traditional rules of the Imperial Parliament. She had experienced a string of failed love affairs in her private life - a handsome officer from Osterland was beheaded by a Chaos warband, a poet from Talabek was killed by lightning while reciting love poems outside her bedroom window, and her official marriage was a long and cold mutual tolerance. She had no interest in the countryside of Wesenland - leaving the sheep farmers and quarrying miners to her subordinates - but Nuln was her true passion. She governed Nuln by not governing: leaving the Imperial Engineering Academy to manage the cannon factories, the Merchant Guilds to handle trade disputes, the School of Magic to discipline the battle mages, and she herself ensured that the annual New Year's Eve Masquerade Ball held at the Imperial Palace was always the most coveted invitation on the Old World's social calendar.
